explore_lenses.title: Sabotage affected more than retail fridges
explore_lenses.summary: French authorities say the October 11-12 intrusion altered industrial refrigeration settings at roughly 700 retail sites, causing food losses and some fires. The same investigation also identified other food-sector and small hydroelectric targets.

claims.text: France’s Foreign Ministry said the campaign hit refrigeration controllers at more than 700 French retail locations, causing major material damage, fires and food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros.

ANSSI said compromised equipment had its defrost settings raised to high temperatures; it recorded at least 15 fire starts and said victims also included small butcher shops, an abattoir and cooperative food plants.
ANSSI said the campaign also targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small French hydroelectric installations, though it described the effects there as limited.

explore_lenses.summary: France attributes the sabotage to Shahid Kaveh, which it describes as an IRGC-linked offensive cyber unit. Officials present the refrigerator operation as part of a longer pattern of Iran-linked activity against French interests rather than an isolated incident.

claims.text: The French cyber-crisis coordination body (C4) said it attributed the destructive actions to Shahid Kaveh based on infrastructure characteristics, signing tools, amplification by a propaganda outlet linked to the unit, and Persian-language traces in attack infrastructure.
France’s CERT-FR says C4 comprises ANSSI, COMCYBER, the DGA, DGSE and DGSI, and says the refrigeration attack was an unprecedented French-targeted sabotage operation in scale and aggressiveness.

French authorities say IRGC-linked cyber activity against French interests has been observed since at least 2020, citing attacks connected to Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and an attempted compromise of a French digital-signage operator before the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Reporting said 11 jurors favored acquittal on the murder charges and one favored conviction, leading to the mistrial.

The mistrial did not resolve that disagreement; a new factfinder could evaluate the evidence differently.

sections.heading: French Election Rules Test Bid
sections.body: To appear on the official presidential candidate list, Riner must obtain endorsements from at least 500 national or local elected officials, which are validated by the Constitutional Council. facts.value: The attack occurred shortly after 3 p.m. on 7 November 2026 near Sławkowska Street by Krakow’s Main Market Square (Rynek Główny).

facts.value: Krakow city authorities reported six deaths and 15 injuries in the shooting.

facts.label: Suspect and police response
facts.value: The city said the alleged attacker, identified by police as a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by officers after the incident.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation covering the killing of six people in Krakow and attempted killings of others, including police officers; prosecutors described the Krakow act as a terrorism-related crime.

facts.label: Official mourning
facts.value: Poland declared national mourning for 8–9 November 2026 in tribute to the victims; Krakow separately announced city mourning through 11 November.

event_overview.title: About Egypt Train Safety
event_overview.subject: Egypt Train Safety
event_overview.summary: Egypt Train Safety refers here to the November 8, 2026 collision between two passenger trains in El-Ayyat district, Giza Governorate, south of Cairo. The crash renewed attention on the safety, oversight and modernization of Egypt’s national rail system; the cause and any responsibility remained under investigation as of November 9.

facts.label: Trains and preliminary circumstances
facts.value: Egyptian National Railways identified the trains as No. 134 on the Giza–Fayoum route and No. 2010 on the Cairo–Aswan route. Initial site findings indicated that No. 134 struck the rear of No. 2010 while the latter was stationary on the same track.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: Egypt’s Public Prosecution opened an investigation and ordered a specialized technical committee to examine the site, rolling stock and track, determine technical causes, and assess compliance with operating procedures and safety requirements.

facts.label: Railway governance and safety regulation
facts.value: Egypt’s railways operate under Ministry of Transport supervision. The Ministry’s Railway Safety Regulatory Unit acts as regulator for railway and metro transport, including developing national safety regulations and approving operators’ safety rules and procedures.

facts.label: Modernization context
facts.value: Egypt has pursued railway safety improvements through track renewal and signaling modernization; a World Bank-supported railway project was designed to improve reliability, efficiency and safety on targeted network sections and closed on December 31, 2020.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine conflict is an armed conflict centered on Ukraine that began with Russia’s occupation of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine in 2014, then expanded sharply when Russian forces launched a full-scale attack on 24 February 2022. It has combined conventional military operations, occupation and territorial-control disputes, humanitarian consequences, and national and international criminal-law investigations.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Russia began occupying Ukrainian territory in Crimea in February 2014; armed conflict subsequently developed in parts of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Russia launched its full-scale armed attack against Ukraine on 24 February 2022.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict concerns Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, including Crimea and areas affected by hostilities or Russian occupation in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Kherson, Luhansk, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions.

facts.label: United Nations position
facts.value: In resolution ES-11/1, adopted on 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and demanded that Russia cease its use of force and withdraw its military forces from Ukraine.

facts.label: International criminal-law process
facts.value: The International Criminal Court opened its Ukraine investigation on 2 March 2022 after referrals by States Parties. Its stated scope covers alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide committed by any person on Ukrainian territory from 21 November 2013 onward.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission has documented civilian deaths, injuries, displacement, and damage to homes, schools, health facilities and other civilian infrastructure resulting from the full-scale hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights specific cross-border criminal or security cases involving foreign nationals allegedly joining or assisting either side; it does not provide a complete record of battlefield developments, diplomacy, humanitarian conditions, or all conflict-related prosecutions.
